topics.intro: Words from the Year 3 and 4 list. These are real challenges for a Year 2 speller!
topics.talk: Ask {him} to spell “island” and spot the silent letter.

topics.title: Adding endings: -ing, -ed, -er, -est
topics.intro: When you add an ending, sometimes the word changes: hop → hopping (double the p), happy → happier (y becomes i).
topics.talk: Ask {him}: what is the -ing word for “run”? For “smile”?

topics.title: Endings: -ful, -less, -ness, -ment, -ly
topics.intro: Suffixes change what a word means: help → helpful → helpless. Watch out: -ful has only one l!
topics.talk: Make as many words as you can from “play” (playful, player, playing…).

topics.title: Words that sound the same
topics.intro: Homophones sound the same but are spelt differently and mean different things: sea and see, knight and night.
topics.talk: Ask {him} to spell “night” and “knight” and explain which is which.

head: Sound the same
Mean different things
rows: the ocean / look with your eyes
a soldier in armour / when it is dark
with your ear / in this place

topics.title: Nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs
topics.intro: Words have jobs. Nouns name things. Verbs are doing words. Adjectives describe nouns. Adverbs describe how something is done.
topics.teach: Find a noun, a verb and an adjective in: “The red car zoomed.”
topics.talk: Ask {him} for three adjectives to describe a superhero.

visual.caption: The adjective describes the noun. The adverb tells you HOW they dance.

topics.title: Full stops, question marks and exclamation marks
topics.intro: Every sentence starts with a capital letter. A statement ends with a full stop, a question with a question mark, and an exclamation with an exclamation mark!
topics.teach: Explain the difference between a statement, a question and a command.
topics.talk: Ask {him} to make up a question about space.

topics.title: Apostrophes
topics.intro: An apostrophe can show missing letters (do not → don’t) or that something belongs to someone (the dog’s bone).
topics.talk: Find an apostrophe on a shop sign and ask what it is doing.

visual.caption: The apostrophe goes where the missing letters were.

topics.title: Joining words and tenses
topics.intro: Joining words (conjunctions) like and, but, because and when make longer, better sentences. Tense tells us when something happens: past, present or future.
topics.talk: Start a sentence and ask {him} to finish it: “I was happy because…”

items.prompt: Which word means “without hope”?
Which word fits? “The pirate ship sailed across the ___.”

options.feedback: “see” is what you do with your eyes.

items.explain: sea (the ocean) and see (with your eyes) sound the same.

items.prompt: Which word fits? “The ___ wore shining armour.”

options.feedback: “night” is when it is dark. A knight with a silent k is a soldier on a horse.

items.explain: knight (a soldier) and night (dark time) sound the same.

items.prompt: Which word fits? “I have ___ racing cars.”

options.feedback: “to” is for going somewhere: to the shop.

items.explain: two (2), to (towards) and too (also / too much).

items.prompt: Which word fits? “The children put on ___ helmets.”
items.explain: their = belonging to them. Their has “heir” inside it, someone who gets things.

items.prompt: Which word fits? “The wind ___ the leaves away.”
items.explain: blew (past of blow) and blue (colour) sound the same.

items.prompt: Which word fits? “The ___ shone brightly in the sky.”

options.feedback: A son is a boy in a family.

items.explain: sun (in the sky) and son (a boy) sound the same.

items.explain: won (past of win) and one (1) sound the same.

options.feedback: “here” is a place. You hear with your ear: there is an “ear” in hear!

options.feedback: “bare” means with nothing on: bare feet.

items.explain: bear (the animal) and bare (uncovered) sound the same.

items.prompt: Which word is a noun (a naming word)?

options.feedback: quickly tells you how: it is an adverb.
shiny describes something: it is an adjective.
zoom is something you do: a verb.

items.explain: A noun names a person, place or thing: rocket, castle, hero.

items.prompt: Which word is a verb (a doing word)?
items.explain: Verbs are actions: jumped, flies, races.

items.prompt: Which word is an adjective (a describing word)?
items.explain: Adjectives describe nouns: an enormous robot.

items.prompt: Which word is an adverb (it tells you HOW)?

options.feedback: quiet is an adjective. Add -ly to make the adverb: quietly.

items.explain: Many adverbs end in -ly: quietly, quickly, bravely.

items.prompt: In “The brave hero rescued the tiny kitten”, which two words are adjectives?
items.explain: brave describes the hero; tiny describes the kitten.

items.prompt: Find the verb: “Turbo zoomed past the finish line.”

options.feedback: Turbo is a name: a noun.

items.prompt: Which is the best expanded noun phrase?
items.explain: An expanded noun phrase adds describing words: the shiny silver rocket.

items.prompt: Which sentence needs a question mark?

options.feedback: That tells you something: it is a statement.

items.explain: Questions ask something and end with ?.

items.prompt: Which is an exclamation?

options.text: What a fast car that is!

items.explain: In grammar, an exclamation starts with “What” or “How”, has a verb, and shows strong feeling: What a fast car that is!

items.prompt: Which is a command (it tells you to do something)?
items.explain: Commands start with a bossy verb: Put, Go, Stop, Look.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?

options.text: On Monday, Sam went to London.
on monday, sam went to london.
options.feedback: Sentences, days, names and places all need capitals.

options.text: On monday, Sam went to london.
options.feedback: Monday and London are names, so they need capitals too.

items.explain: Capitals for the start of a sentence, names, days, months and places, and the word I.

items.prompt: Where do the commas go in this list? “I saw a rocket a planet a star and a moon.”

options.text: I saw a rocket, a planet, a star and a moon.
I saw a rocket a planet, a star, and, a moon.
options.feedback: Commas go between the items, but not before “and” in a simple list.

options.text: I saw, a rocket a planet a star and a moon.
options.feedback: The commas separate the items in the list.

items.explain: Use commas between items in a list, and “and” before the last one.

items.prompt: Which word always needs a capital letter, wherever it is in a sentence?
items.explain: “I” is always a capital: Ben and I raced. Names, days, months and places need capitals too.

items.prompt: What is the short form of “do not”?
items.explain: The apostrophe goes where the missing letter was: do n(o)t → don’t.

options.feedback: You need an apostrophe to show it belongs.
Just one apostrophe, before the s.

items.explain: Add ’s to show something belongs to someone: the driver’s helmet.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

options.feedback: Plurals do NOT need an apostrophe.
No apostrophe for a simple plural.

items.explain: Only use an apostrophe for missing letters or belonging, never just to make a plural.

items.prompt: Choose the best joining word: “The hero was tired ___ he had flown all night.”
Choose the best joining word: “Blaze was fast ___ Turbo was faster.”

options.feedback: There is no reason here: it is a contrast.

items.explain: “but” shows a contrast between two ideas.

items.prompt: Choose the best joining word: “The crowd cheered ___ Turbo won.”
items.explain: “when” tells you the time something happened.

items.prompt: Choose the best joining word: “You can play ___ you finish your tea.”

options.feedback: This is a condition, not a reason.

items.prompt: Which sentence is in the past tense?

options.text: The rocket will land on Mars.

items.explain: Past tense verbs often end in -ed: landed.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows something happening right now?
items.explain: “is dancing” is the present progressive: happening now.

items.prompt: What is the past tense of “run”?
items.explain: run is irregular: today I run, yesterday I ran.

items.prompt: What is the past tense of “fly”?
items.explain: fly → flew. (“I have flown” uses a helper word.)

sentences.title: Ask a question
sentences.prompt: Write a question you would ask an astronaut.

checks.msg: A question ends with a question mark (?).

sentences.model: What does Earth look like from space?
sentences.tip: Questions often start with What, Where, When, Why, How or Who.

sentences.title: Use “because”
sentences.prompt: Finish this sentence with a reason: “I love racing cars because…”
sentences.model: I love racing cars because they are fast and colourful.
sentences.tip: “because” is always followed by a reason.

sentences.title: Two describing words
sentences.prompt: Write a sentence about a superhero using TWO adjectives (describing words), like “brave” and “strong”.
sentences.model: The brave, strong hero flew over the city.
sentences.tip: Put adjectives before the noun: the brave hero.

sentences.title: An exclamation
sentences.prompt: Write an exclamation that starts with “What” about a rocket. End it with an exclamation mark.
sentences.model: What a gigantic rocket that is!
sentences.tip: Exclamations show strong feelings: What a…! How…!

sentences.title: A list with commas
sentences.prompt: Write a sentence listing three things you would take to space. Use commas and “and”.

checks.msg: Use a comma between the first items in your list.

sentences.model: I would take a torch, a teddy and a sandwich.
sentences.tip: Commas between items, then “and” before the last one.

sentences.title: Use “when”
sentences.prompt: Write a sentence using “when”, like “I smile when…”
sentences.model: I smile when I win a race.
sentences.tip: “when” joins two ideas and tells you the time.

sentences.title: Past tense
sentences.prompt: Write a sentence about something you did yesterday. Use the past tense (like “played” or “went”).

checks.msg: Use a past tense verb, like played, went or saw.

sentences.model: Yesterday I played football in the park.
sentences.tip: Past tense verbs often end in -ed, but some are special: went, saw, ran.

sentences.title: Use “but”
sentences.prompt: Write a sentence using “but”: “The robot was small but…”
sentences.model: The robot was small but very clever.
sentences.tip: “but” shows a surprise: two ideas that don’t usually go together.
